scope: Bounded write/change/restore preparation for exact VDensHO1 / 20C2 / SW03 maintenance configuration. Reset paths remain excluded.

0x5721.side_effect: Live CLI test: changing 0 -> nonzero threshold re-baselined read-only 0x7570 to current burner runtime. Restore nonzero -> 0 did not re-baseline it in the observed capture.

0x5723.access: read+write (same global Vitosoft event; exact VDensHO1 generated catalog is deduplicated to the diagnostic read presentation)

0x5724.access: read+write status enum in generated catalog
0x5724.caveat: Live tests confirm state 00 -> 01 -> 00 and re-baselining of 0x756C. The effect on 0x7570 is conditional: an early reset initialized a zero burner reference, while a later CLI reset with 0x5721=0 h left an existing 0x7570 reference unchanged.

0x756C.interpretation: custom 32-bit LastCheckInterval reference; not a plain month counter; exact wall-clock conversion remains unresolved

0x7570.interpretation: read-only burner-runtime baseline in raw seconds; elapsed burner hours since the current maintenance reference = (current 0x08A7 raw seconds - stored 0x7570 raw seconds) / 3600. It can be updated by changing 0x5721 and was initialized by an earlier 0x5724 reset, but a later 0x5724 reset with 0x5721=0 h left it unchanged.

probe_plan.required_sequence: baseline reads -> write 24 -> readback and side-effect reads -> restore 0 -> final reads
probe_plan.stop_condition: Do not proceed to phase B if 0x5724 becomes nonzero, either counter changes unexpectedly, write/readback fails, or restore-to-zero is not confirmed.

probe_plan.required_sequence: baseline reads -> write raw 100 -> readback and side-effect reads -> restore raw 0 -> final reads
probe_plan.stop_condition: Do not run until 0x5724 reset behavior and 0x7570 LastBurnerCheck side effects are bounded.

excluded_operations: No Home Assistant command topic until live change/readback/restore semantics are verified.

interval_reference_decode.note: Little-endian integers differed by exactly 10 over a 10-second interval. Do not treat them as verified Unix timestamps.

conclusions: 0x5723 is locally verified read/write for the source-backed 0..24 month range.
0x756C changed to a new seconds-like 32-bit LastCheckInterval reference on both setting changes; exact wall-clock conversion is unresolved.
0x756C is therefore not a plain elapsed-month integer.
0x5724 stayed at Grundzustand and 0x7570 stayed zero.
0x5724 readback followed 00 -> 01 -> 00.
The transition back to 00 updated both maintenance reference registers.
0x756C stores a time reference.
0x7570 stores a burner-runtime reference matching the total-runtime register within two seconds.
0x08A7 and 0x088A remained unchanged.
0x5721 is locally verified read/write.
Decimal raw write value 100 produced register byte 0x64, corresponding to 10000 h via raw * 100 h.
Restore to raw 0 was successful.
This early probe did not visibly change 0x7570 because it ran immediately after the maintenance reset; a later live CLI test proved that changing 0x5721 from 0 to nonzero can re-baseline 0x7570.
Changing 0x5721 does not alter total burner runtime 0x08A7 or burner starts 0x088A.
0x5721 and 0x5723 are independently configurable thresholds, but each can re-baseline its corresponding maintenance reference; 0x5724 1->0 re-baselines both.

reset_source.behavior: If maintenance is performed before the service indication appears, set coding 24:1 and then 24:0; maintenance parameters for burner hours and time interval start again at zero.
reset_source.separation: Resetting total burner operating hours, burner starts and consumption is a separate optional service operation.
reset_source.implication: A bounded 0x5724 1 -> 0 sequence is source-backed as the maintenance-interval reset path; total counters should be monitored but must not be intentionally reset.

next_probe.expected_research_value: If 0x7570 snapshots 0x08A7 when 24 is reset, LastBurnerCheck can be modeled as current total burner runtime minus stored maintenance baseline.

write.0x5721: verified R/W, raw 0..100 corresponds to 0..10000 h in 100 h steps; changing 0->nonzero can re-baseline 0x7570
write.0x5723: verified R/W, raw 0..24 corresponds to 0..24 months

reset.effect: 0x5724 1 -> 0 reliably re-baselines 0x756C; 0x7570 effect is conditional on controller/configuration state and must not be assumed.

read_only_references.0x756C: 32-bit LastCheckInterval reference; seconds-like behavior verified, exact wall-clock conversion unresolved

corrections.subject: 0x756C LastCheckInterval wall-clock interpretation
corrections.finding: Earlier notes called the little-endian value a Unix timestamp. Live CLI output exposed a wall-clock mismatch, and public Vitosoft reverse-engineering documentation lists LastCheckInterval as a special converter whose algorithm is not implemented. Keep the field raw until the converter is reconstructed.

set_hours_zero.note: Only reads were issued; no WRITE 0x5721 occurred.

set_months_zero.note: Only reads were issued; no WRITE 0x5723 occurred and the LastCheckInterval reference was preserved.

ERROR: set-hours accepts 0..10000 h in exact 100 h steps

set_100_hours.finding: Changing 0x5721 from 0 h to 100 h re-baselined 0x7570 to the current burner-runtime counter.

restore_0_hours.finding: Restoring 0x5721 from 100 h to 0 h did not re-baseline 0x7570 again in this capture.

interpretation: The earlier raw 0x5721 probe occurred immediately after a maintenance reset, so a possible re-baseline of 0x7570 was masked by an already-current reference.
A real later CLI write made the side effect visible: enabling a nonzero burner-hours threshold can restart the burner-hours maintenance reference.
The CLI must require explicit acknowledgement before any actual 0x5721 write.
Do not describe (0x08A7-0x7570)/3600 as proof of elapsed time since a physical maintenance event; it is elapsed burner runtime since the current maintenance reference.

conclusions: The guarded CLI set-months path is live-verified for write, readback and restore.
Every actual 0x5723 write re-baselines only the LastCheckInterval reference at 0x756C.
0x7570 remains unchanged by 0x5723 changes.
The reference advanced by 6 counts across the approximately 6-second set-to-zero restore interval, reinforcing seconds-like behavior without asserting a wall-clock epoch.
The guarded CLI reset path is live-verified end-to-end, including 0x5724 readback 00 -> 01 -> 00 and final Grundzustand.
0x756C was re-baselined by the maintenance reset.
0x7570 remained unchanged in this reset capture while the configured burner-hours threshold 0x5721 was 0 h.
The earlier reset capture initialized 0x7570 from zero, so the burner-reference effect of 0x5724 is not unconditional and must be reported as controller-state/configuration dependent.
0x08A7 and 0x088A did not decrease or reset.
End-to-end read-only MQTT API path is live-verified: client -> maintenance command topic -> API service -> shared core -> splitter -> result topic.
The CLI still returns the same maintenance status after the core refactor.
The shared maintenance lock is provisioned with permissions usable by both root CLI and the optolink API service.

safe_behavior_suite.deduplication: Repeated request_id returned the cached result with deduplicated=true.
safe_behavior_suite.guards: set_hours 100, set_months 1 and reset were rejected without confirmation.

conclusions: The root CLI and unprivileged MQTT API contend on the same advisory lock.
Both frontends fail closed with a busy error while the lock is held.
Normal CLI access resumes immediately after the lock is released.
The MQTT API write path is live-verified end-to-end with a bounded set_months write and restore.
Both writes were independently read back and both re-baselined only 0x756C.
0x7570, 0x5721, 0x5724, 0x08A7 and 0x088A remained unchanged throughout the API write/restore test.
The maintenance backend is ready for Home Assistant integration; no further backend write experiments are required.
Home Assistant staging topics are live-verified to be non-writing.
Changing staged maintenance targets does not acquire a controller write path and leaves 0x5721/0x5723 unchanged.
The staged values were subsequently returned to 0 h / 0 months.
